requiresInput.prompt: What is the current climate or season?

results.description:
During a blizzard, the group's daily travel speed is reduced by 2 hexes. At the end of each hour a human spends outside without cold weather gear, they make a Strength RR.
2d10 + S
1  They take 4d6 P dam.
2  They take 3d6 P dam.
3  They take 2d6 P dam.
A creature takes a cumulative -2 penalty to this test for each time they've previously made this test before donning cold weather gear, taking shelter, or experiencing a change in the weather.
Guides, scouts, and trackers take a double bane on tests made to fulfill their roles during the blizzard.

During a cold snap, at the end of each hour a human spends outside without cold weather gear, they make a Strength RR.
2d10 + S
1  They take 3d6 P dam.
2  They take 2d6 P dam.
3  They take 1d6 P dam.
A creature takes a cumulative -2 penalty to this test for each time they previously made this test before donning cold weather gear, taking shelter, or experiencing a change in the weather.

During a heat wave, if a creature travels more than 2 hexes in a day, they must make a Strength RR.
2d10 + S
1  They take 2d6 P dam.
2  They take 1d6 P dam.
3  No effect.
During a sandstorm, the group's travel speed is reduced by 2 hexes. Guides, scouts, and trackers take a double bane on tests made to fulfill their roles during a sandstorm.

In the rain, the group's travel speed is reduced by 1 hex. Creatures carrying rations must make the following Mind test.
2d10 + M
1  They lose 1d6 + 1 rations to mold.
2  They lose 1 ration to mold.
3  No effect.

results.text: Roll twice — merchant operates as two different institutions
1 Blood Creature C and 1d6 Blood Creature A
Asleep — unconscious in the PCs' path. Waking the animal causes them to become violent.
Attached — inexplicably attracted to a randomly chosen PC. Follows and is friendly toward that PC, but frightened of all others.
Curious — approaches cautiously but openly. Aggressive behavior causes fright; calm behavior causes them to investigate then leave; sharing food makes them friendly.
Embattled — pick or roll on an encounter table for other animals, humans, or monsters battling the animals. If the PCs aid the original group, one animal becomes friendly.
Friendly — happily follows the PCs for an hour. A PC can make a test to become the animal's owner. Mean or aggressive behavior causes them to flee.

Frightened — freezes and stares at the PCs. Anything other than utmost calm causes flight (if outmatched and has a way out) or fighting until PCs flee (if cornered). A Mind test with Handle Animal can turn attitude to curious.
Hungry — approaches when PCs are eating. If given ≥1 ration, becomes friendly. If not fed, attacks to steal food and flee.
Injured — Stamina equal to half maximum, visibly hurt. Frightened and considered cornered, but any PC who heals them turns their attitude to friendly.
Playful — wants to catch sticks, be chased, wrestle, etc. Approaches energetically. If PCs engage in play, becomes friendly. If not, becomes violent.

Protective — guarding something; attacks any creature who approaches it; fights to the death. Roll any die: even = defending a nest with 1d10 babies or eggs (each sellable to a village stables as a pet). Odd = protecting one thing from the Minor Interesting Things table.
Stalking — follows the PCs from hidden positions. Waits until one or two PCs are alone, then pounces.
Starved — desperate for food. Approaches aggressively. Attacks unless given a full day's worth of food (by size), then flees. Carnivores may attempt to kill and carry off a PC if not fed.
Territorial — follows the PCs displaying aggression but never closing in. Stops pursuing when PCs exit the hex where the encounter occurred. If the PCs stop moving, attacks and fights to the death.
Treasure-Seeking — attracted to something a PC wears or holds (often shiny or looks like food). Makes its interest clear; attacks if not given the item.
Violent — out for blood due to past trauma or incurable infection. Ambushes and attacks the PCs.

Animal Hunt — travelers hunt an animal on the appropriate habitat table. If the PCs help, reward from Traveler Rewards.
Battle — travelers battling 2d6 Miasma-touched humans. Roll 1d6: 1–2 bandits, 3–4 cannibals, 5–6 cultists. If PCs save the travelers, reward from Traveler Rewards.
Camping — travelers camping, welcoming PCs with caution. Friendly PCs are offered a shared meal (skip rations next rest). Standoffish PCs are asked to leave.
Crows — another crow group heading to a nearby dungeon. Roll 1d6: 1–2 invite PCs along; 3–4 standoffish but share lore if PCs are kind; 5–6 view PCs as rivals and plan to kill them.
Injured — one or more travelers has 1d6 wounds and an injured leg. If PCs heal them or provide a mount, reward from Traveler Rewards.
Lost — travelers are lost. If PCs spend a day guiding them, reward from Traveler Rewards.
Need an Escort — survivors of a monster attack need escort to the nearest village. If PCs agree, reward from Traveler Rewards.
Pursued by Monsters — travelers chased by monsters from the nearest dungeon's encounter table. If PCs intervene, travelers flee, leaving their dead behind.
Starving — travelers are out of food. If PCs provide 1d6 days of food, reward from Traveler Rewards.
Treasure Hunt — travelers searching for a specific item (perhaps from Major Interesting Things). If PCs help and hand over the item, reward from Traveler Rewards.
Nothing — the travelers have nothing to give, or consider virtue its own reward. Jerks.
A piece of useful information about a nearby POI, dungeon, village, or treasure.
An item from the Minor Interesting Things table
An item from the Major Interesting Things table
Bandits — threaten to kill PCs unless given 10d10 × 10 gc worth of goods. Only attack if refused and they believe they have the advantage.
Cannibals — want to eat the PCs. If they outnumber the PCs, ambush them. Otherwise pose as fellow travelers, then attack when PCs are vulnerable.
Competitive — challenge PCs to a contest (strength, foot race, trivia) with a wager. Gracious winner/loser = they leave. Disagreement or gloating = attack.
Cruel — revel in cruelty. 50% chance they've captured a creature to torture. Otherwise approach as friendly, planning to kidnap a PC.
Cultists — cult of a Necromancer. Trade anything for necromancy spellbooks. Attempt to convert PCs; attack those who've stolen from or insulted their Necromancer.
Death to the Gods — hate all religion. If any PCs carry religious material, wait for an opportune moment to attack them. Agreeable PCs may receive assistance, though the NPCs won't enter towns.
Deceitful — fabricate tales about nearby monsters, dungeons, and landmarks. Lure believers into traps. If accused of lying, attack (if confident) or flee.
Despondent — trudge through the world crying and upset. Defend themselves if threatened; lash out verbally then physically at anyone who tries to comfort them.
Destructive — confrontational, trying to bait a fight. Give their anger a direction and they go destroy it. Otherwise they battle the PCs.
False Bravado — claim to be brave crows seeking treasure. Invite PCs to join them. Actually cowards who run off when any fight starts.
Greedy — want food, shelter, supplies, and treasure for as little effort as possible. Appear as beggars if PCs are stronger; as bandits if PCs can be bullied.
Knowledge Seeker — want lore books and expert conversations. Stop PCs and pepper them with questions. Attack if PCs try to leave, planning to kidnap the most knowledgeable.
Mage Hunter — ambush PCs openly carrying spellbooks. If none, ask if PCs know of any mages. Goal: kill magic users and claim their spellbooks.
Monster Hatred — hate a specific monster type in a nearby dungeon or POI. Ask PCs to help kill them. Rush in recklessly as soon as monsters are encountered.
Monster Obsessed — love a specific monster nearby. Lure PCs inside with treasure rumors. The place is rigged with bear traps for their favorite monsters.
Sluggish — claim to be lost, want to find civilization. Actually aimless wanderers who slow the group by 1 hex/day. Leave happily at a village. If abandoned, ambush PCs on next outdoor encounter.
Suspicious — friendly at first, then quickly suspicious of the PCs' intentions. Flee if outmatched; follow and ambush the PCs' camp if they believe they can win.
Thieves — befriend PCs while sizing up their possessions. Steal one or more valuable items and flee when an opportunity arises.

Tyrant — one leader whom the others worship. Demands fealty from all; kills those who refuse. Grants a blessing to those who swear loyalty. Next time this encounter is rolled, the group demands a progress update.
Vain — value appearance above all. Praise well-groomed PCs; suggest a bath to dirty ones; plot to kidnap and clean those who refuse.
Violent — attack PCs on the road, offering to stop if just one PC agrees to die for the others.
Wicked Crows — corrupted crows who offer to raid a dungeon together. Once inside, they systematically use the dungeon's horrors to eliminate the PCs one by one.
